newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling makes gains against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling makes gains against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling made marginal gains against the dollar on Thursday in a moderately active market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.74 against the dollar from 55.76 on Wednesday, while on the pound it was posted at a weaker 89.06 from 88.56 on Wednesday.
Dealers said the shilling gained marginally amid thin inflows with exporters holding on to their dollars due to unattractive prices and subdued importer demand.
"Traders tried to match their positions internally with the dollar holding firm at the 55.70/80 level as dollar sales thinned," a dealer said.

Another dealer said the market was at a standstill with no trade incentive from either side. "For as long as the shilling continues to appreciate against the dollar, importer demand will remain subdued.
"Normally, importers try to cover their positions forward as the year draws to an end. Unfortunately for them, the current rate is expensive," he added.
A commercial banker said that unless the shilling went up to the 58.50 level in the next three months, the market was likely to see importer demand stay subdued.
Liquidity in the money market was low with most of the banks seeking for funds. Rates were quoted at above 25 percent from 22-24 percent on Wednesday.
